evidence.note: Thesis up front: 'A shared rooftop array could undercut what blocks C and D pay for daytime power'.
'About 40% of what flats on blocks C and D spend on electricity falls in daylight hours' quantifies the daytime spend the thesis targets.
'26 of the 33 households that answered the survey support a pilot' adds resident demand; a slight pivot from cost to support but still a finding.
'A 12-month pilot tests savings and upkeep on two roofs first' states the proposal following from support.
'One shared array per roof feeds the block's landlord supply' explains how the pilot delivers the saving.
'Roof leaks, falling tariffs and later upkeep are the pilot's main risks' names the risks as a finding, not a label.
'The board is asked to approve the £86,400 pilot, with a go or stop review at twelve months' closes with the ask, echoing s-4 without repeating it.

rationale: Every title is a stated finding, the thesis opens the deck, and the sequence runs claim, evidence of cost, resident support, proposal, mechanism, risks, ask. The s-2 to s-3 step shifts from cost to support but still advances the case, and s-7 restates the pilot only to frame the decision. Read alone, the titles summarise the talk with no repetition or gap.
